methods.label: Interpret the logarithm and factor
methods.explanation:
A base-10 logarithm equals \(1\) precisely when its argument equals \(10^1=10\). Thus the equation becomes
\[
x^2-3x+6=10,
\]
or
\[
x^2-3x-4=(x-4)(x+1)=0.
\]
A product is zero only if at least one factor is zero, so \(x=4\) or \(x=-1\). Both values make the original logarithm argument equal to \(10>0\), so both are valid. The answer is \(\boxed{4\text{ or }-1}\), choice D.
